chunks: Destiny holds sway over predetermination till effort itself brings about ruin.

key_terms.الآفَةُ: Ruin, destruction, or the source of a flaw/failure.
key_terms.التَّدْبِيرِ: Management, planning, or effort exerted by the individual.
key_terms.التَّقْدِيرِ: Predetermination or the act of measuring/estimating, often referring to human planning or limited scope.
key_terms.الْمِقْدَارُ: Divine decree or destiny, referring to God's ultimate determination of events.

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine decree and human effort in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the dynamic between divine decree (al-miqdār) and human effort (al-tadbīr), noting that while planning is necessary, it is ultimately subject to God's will. This highlights a key Shia theological nuance: human agency is real but subordinate to the overarching divine plan, meaning that even the most prudent management can lead to ruin if it contradicts the ultimate divine measure. This serves as a reminder for believers to combine diligent effort with reliance on God (tawakkul), recognizing that outcomes are not solely determined by human calculation.
